summary: Moss starts checking in on your day, lands on Android, and learns to answer with cards for weather, sports, tasks and reminders.
intro: This was a big week. Moss can now speak up on its own when something in your day needs attention, it has a proper Android app, and a lot of chat answers now come with a card you can read at a glance. The ring got much faster too, and the fixes are at the bottom if that's all you're here for.

headline.title: Moss checks in on your day
body: Moss can now post a short check-in in your Main chat when something in your tasks, calendar, memory, sports or news needs your attention. When nothing has changed, it stays quiet. You choose how often it looks and which of those sources it may read, all from Settings.

Each check-in has a thumbs up and a thumbs down, and you can tell Moss to stop bringing up a topic (and change your mind later). Times in check-ins show in your own timezone, written the way a person would say them.

items.title: Moss for Android
items.body: Moss now has an Android app that opens Moss full screen. Ring settings live under Settings, Connections, Hardware, where you'll find delivery, ring status, storage and connection help in one place. You can connect a ring you already own, look through its saved recordings, and stop any single one from being sent.

items.title: Answers you can see
items.body: Ask about the weather and Moss draws an hourly forecast with a temperature curve, icons, rain and wind. Ask about your team and it shows the latest result with logos and the score. Questions about tasks and reminders get a tidy card with due dates, times and status, and facts you share in chat can become a labelled visual summary. Every card says where its information came from.

items.title: Every kind of recording
items.body: Meetings now takes more than meetings. Paste in a transcript and Moss will name it, pick a type, and label it personal or work. You can then change or filter that type yourself. You can also ask Moss in chat to add, rename or retire recording types and choose how each one gets summarised. When Moss isn't sure whether a recording is personal or work, it says so in Main with a link to review it.

items.title: Transcripts that know your words
items.body: Save spellings for names and terms, and Moss will use them to guide future meeting transcripts as well as your audio service allows. You can also set the spoken language for new transcripts or let it be detected automatically. Admins can choose one transcription provider and model for everyone.

items.title: A much faster ring
items.body: Holding the ring button to talk now gets a reply in about 15 seconds instead of around 50. Voice requests are picked up sooner and queued ones carry on the moment Moss is free. Ring messages also flow straight into Main chat without touching your unsent drafts, and quick voice commands no longer show up as meetings.

items.title: A simpler ring app
items.body: The ring app's Home now shows only the thing you need to do next, with everything else gathered in Settings. Ring setup finishes back on your Hardware settings. The reminder for a recording that has run past an hour now pops up with sound and vibration, and repeats every 30 minutes until you dismiss it.

items.title: Tidier AI provider settings
items.body: Adding an AI provider happens in one pop-up, and the settings you rarely touch fold away. OpenCode no longer has its own special card, so it works like every other provider. You can pick the decision model in a simple dialog and lock your own assistant to one model. The Classifier's chat gate can now be switched straight to On.

items.title: Recordings clean up after themselves
items.body: Deleting a recording or your account now clears its linked notes and memories first, and holds back any note you've changed so you can review it. Account exports now include the history behind recording notes and memories.

items.title: Less reading in Settings
items.body: Outlook calendar sits in a compact account row, Connections and Notes repeat themselves less, and Meeting and transcription settings keep their help short.

items.title: Turning off a module asks first
items.body: Before an add-on module is switched off, Moss now asks you to confirm and explains what happens to background jobs still waiting to run.

fixes.text: Long meeting recordings now get a summary instead of failing for being too long.
Meeting summaries keep working after the AI tools behind them update, and they use your chosen default model.
Ring recordings longer than about 45 minutes now reach Moss.
Ring recordings no longer get stuck without a transcript when the ring's clock drifts.
Noisy recordings no longer lose stretches of speech, and transcripts finish even when the speech service runs slightly past the end of the audio.
Excluded ring recordings no longer offer to retry transcription.
Chat keeps following Moss's reply as it's written instead of leaving you scrolled up.
A file you attach stays visible on your message while Moss replies.
Tool results under Moss's thinking steps read as plain text, with no stray symbols.
A stray dot from a near-silent ring press no longer sticks to Main chat, and the interrupted notice clears when you send again.
When a one-time task check can't be scheduled, Moss explains why instead of wandering off into an unrelated reply.
Two note edits that save at the same moment both survive, and Moss flags it when an outside edit collides with a save.
